revenuecatEventReasons.why: Auto-renew was turned off. Access continues to the paid-through date, which is exactly what cancelled_at_period_end names — mapping it to subscription_expired would end access on the day the user pressed cancel.

The subscription reached its end and did not renew. This is the event that actually ends access; the finer expiration_reason sub-field is NOT read here, because a per-sub-reason table would be a second vendor fact nobody has verified.

Play lets a subscriber pause; the row stops being entitled and resumes later. subscription_paused exists in the reason set precisely so a pause is not recorded as an expiry, which would be read as churn.

NOT A REVOCATION. It is a grace-period warning and the store retries; the final outcome arrives later as EXPIRATION. Mapping it to payment_failed_final would lock out a customer whose card recovers, which is the failure this whole table is shaped to avoid.
NOT A REVOCATION — a grant. Recorded so the table is a complete answer for the events the client can see, rather than a list that goes quiet on the ones that matter most.
NOT A REVOCATION — the subscription continued.
NOT A REVOCATION — auto-renew was turned back on before the period ended, so there is nothing to take away.
